newsitem.title: RUSSIA: PLD TELEKOM SET FOR RUSSIAN EARNINGS GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: PLD TELEKOM SET FOR RUSSIAN EARNINGS GROWTH.

text.p: U.S. phone operator PLD Telekom is well poised to benefit from Russia's rapidly growing telecommunications market over the next few years, Moscow investment bank Renaissance Capital said.
The company, which comprises three subsidiaries in Russia and the Central Asian republic of Kazakhstan, currently has negative earnings, it said in a report.
But the report recommended buying the NASDAQ-quoted stock given its capital investments, expanding customer base and strong cash flow.

"Following several years of heavy investment and losses, PLD is finally set to translate subscriber growth into strong earnings performance," the report said, adding it expected PLD to break even in 1998.
Renaissance Capital forecast earnings would jump 2,147 percent in 1999, and said the share price, currently quoted at $6.13, would climb to $10.00 over the next year.

It warned that the rate of progress on a satellite-based long-distance network and debts could affect projected earnings growth, but said management's focus on high-technology services for corporate clients would stand it in good stead.
